findings.rationale: Accepted: the snapshot is a write-once file beside the sealed contract (O_EXCL), identity-checked on read; resume never re-snapshots — a differing live roster is recorded as live_drift and ignored; the live roster never wins at admission, resume or panel.

Accepted: the snapshot stores the admitted seat objects (role, runner, model, effort, endpoint, family) plus seats_complete, minimum, families and implementer family — everything the 2-A prepare step reads — and intake's qualification decision is the sealed one, so finalPanelSeatQualified is not re-run against the live roster; the seats_complete gate reads the snapshot.

Accepted: the terminal object seals sealed_required_review_families and implementer_family; the validator re-derives quorum_met from the rows and those fields and refuses a disagreeing flag (final_panel_quorum_flag_mismatch); load_bearing patterns are checked row by row.
Accepted: the packet-hash all-or-none/one-value rule is scoped to reviewed rows in both engine and validator; failed rows never carry a hash.

Accepted: extraSeat is the duplicate-tuple case (unchanged); the four new fields are OPTIONAL in the schema with legacy (unanimity) semantics when absent, so the nine suites that hand-build seat receipts pass untouched while the engine always emits them and the receipt suite pins that.
Accepted: the full Context string is written out with its byte count (under 240) and Status open; the version is a release-commit pin.
